{{Short description|Russian-American mathematician}}
'''Julia Pevtsova''' is a Russian-American mathematician who works as a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Washington]]. Her research concerns [[representation theory]] and in particular [[modular representation theory]].

Pevtsova competed for Russia in the 1992 [[International Mathematical Olympiad]], earning a silver medal.{{r|cv|imo}}
She earned a bachelor's degree in 1997 from [[Saint Petersburg State University]],{{r|cv}} and completed her doctorate in 2002 at [[Northwestern University]], under the supervision of [[Eric Friedlander]].{{r|cv|mgp}} After postdoctoral studies at the [[University of Oregon]], she joined the University of Washington in 2005.{{r|cv}}

In 2017, she became a [[fellow]] of the [[American Mathematical Society]] "for contributions to modular representation theory".{{r|fams}}
In 2018 she won the distinguished teaching award of the Pacific Northwest Section of the [[Mathematical Association of America]]. The award cited her work teaching problem-solving to undergraduates in preparation for the [[William Lowell Putnam Mathematical Competition]] and her leadership of [[math circle]]s and other activities for local secondary-school students.{{r|pnw}}
